raw_response:
I’m thinking about this year the same way I usually do: keep the wheat-maize land steady, don’t spend too aggressively at the start, and leave some cash for topdressing and irrigation later. I’ve farmed here a long time, so I trust what I’ve seen on my own fields first. Wheat still makes the base of the year for me, maize follows right after harvest, and zucchini is my cash crop on a small piece because it brings in money earlier but needs more watching and more labor. With only 3 people in the house and some off-farm work, I can’t make the whole farm too labor-heavy. I have well water, so if it turns dry I can protect the crop, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate just for peace of mind.

For wheat, I’ll keep the management pretty regular because the crop is already in the ground and this is not the year to experiment much. I’ll watch seedling density, leaf color, and soil moisture. If the stand looks normal, I’ll give one main topdress at jointing and then irrigate when the crop really needs it, mainly jointing and heading, maybe one more light watering if spring stays dry. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll move fast into summer maize on the same land. That turnaround is always tight here, so I won’t do deep tillage, just a quick rotary pass or direct seeding after residue handling, then get the maize in within a few days. For zucchini, I’ll keep only a smaller area because it earns cash but needs frequent picking, fertilizer, and pest control. I’d rather do a manageable area well than spread myself thin.
